title: US Data center real estate outperforms as development expands into new markets
gist: US data center real estate returned 7.1% annualized over three years versus 2.1% for all commercial property (NCREIF), but returns have slowed to 0.4% in Q3 2026 as a heavy construction pipeline and rising build, upgrade and power costs weigh on valuations. Hyperscaler capex is projected at $1.17tn in 2027, development is shifting to secondary Midwest, Southeast and Mountain West markets, and data centers now make up nearly 10% of US CRE transaction volume.

themes.theme: Data center returns: outperformance now moderating

insights.claim: US data center real estate delivered an annualized 7.1% return over the past three years, more than triple the 2.1% return for all US commercial properties, according to NCREIF.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Data centers have been the standout CRE sector, defying the broader commercial real estate slowdown, which explains crowded institutional positioning.
insights.quote: US data centers have defied the broader commercial real estate slowdown, delivering an annualized 7.1% return over the past three years

insights.claim: US data center property returns have moderated sharply, reaching just 0.4% in Q3 2026 and 2.4% over the trailing 12 months.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Momentum in data center real estate is fading; returns are converging toward broader CRE levels, which argues for caution on late entry at current valuations.
insights.quote: data center returns have moderated, reaching just 0.4% in Q3 2026 and 2.4% over the past 12 months
insights.locator: More recently, data center returns have moderated

insights.claim: An elevated construction pipeline and higher costs to build, upgrade, and power facilities have likely weighed on US data center property valuations even though income has remained relatively stable.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: The slowdown comes from valuations, not income: supply growth and cost inflation are compressing appreciation, so watch pipeline deliveries and cap rates rather than rents.
insights.quote: an elevated construction pipeline and higher costs to build, upgrade, and power facilities likely weighed on property valuations despite relatively stable income
insights.locator: More recently, data center returns have moderated

themes.theme: Hyperscaler AI capex as the demand engine

insights.claim: The Bloomberg consensus projects that capital spending by the five major hyperscalers will reach $1.17tn in 2027, nearly three times its 2025 level of $412bn, reflecting accelerated investment in AI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Nearly tripling hyperscaler capex underpins data center demand; any downward revision to the consensus is a key risk for data center real estate and the AI infrastructure supply chain.
insights.quote: capital spending of the five major hyperscalers will reach $1.17tn in 2027, nearly three times its 2025 level of $412bn
insights.locator: The Bloomberg consensus projects capital spending

insights.claim: Secondary markets in the US Midwest, Southeast, and Mountain West are gaining importance for data center supply because power constraints, high costs, and local permitting hurdles limit expansion in established hubs.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Development and land/power value accrue to secondary regions; utilities, landowners and developers there may benefit while legacy hubs face supply limits.
insights.quote: power constraints, high costs, and local permitting hurdles limit expansion in established hubs
insights.locator: Secondary markets in the Midwest, Southeast

insights.claim: AI training workloads are less latency-sensitive than other compute and can be located farther from population centers, which reinforces the shift of US data center development to secondary markets.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Training-heavy demand makes site selection depend on cheap available power rather than proximity to users, so power availability is the key location variable.
insights.quote: Less latency-sensitive AI training can occur farther from population centers, reinforcing this shift.
insights.locator: Secondary markets in the Midwest, Southeast

themes.theme: Cost pressure and institutional capital flows

insights.claim: US data center property capital expenditures nearly doubled to $161 per square foot in 2025, showing how expensive it is to maintain and upgrade existing facilities amid rising development, equipment, and property improvement costs.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Rising capex erodes net returns for data center owners; obsolescence risk in older facilities is real, so favor newer assets or those with capex already funded.
insights.quote: Property capital expenditures nearly doubled to $161 per square foot in 2025
insights.locator: Rising development, equipment, and property improvement

insights.claim: Large portfolio and entity acquisitions have lifted data centers' share of US commercial real estate transaction volume to nearly 10%, compared with less than 2% historically, according to MSCI.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Institutional capital has crowded into data centers; at a fivefold jump in deal share alongside slowing returns, the sector looks heavily owned and sensitive to any demand disappointment.
